items.title: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany
items.description: According to a joint press release from the Darmstadt Public Prosecutor's Office and the South Hesse Police Headquarters, Mohamed Aweys Muudey, 68, an asylum seeker who had fled Somalia, was stabbed inside his communal accommodation by a 28-year-old suspect who is now in police custody. Muudey left Somalia in search of safety and protection. However, his life was cut short in a violent knife attack, highlighting the dangers many journalists in exile continue to face. He spent several years in prison in Ethiopia where he was arrested while seeking protection in 2014 before he was pardoned. Muud
items.titleIt: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany

items.title: SJS mourns Somali radio journalist Hassan Kafi Qoyste who died at 57
items.description: Ayanle Hassan, Qoyste's son, told SJS that his father, who was diabetic, fell ill on Friday night and was rushed to hospital, where he was pronounced dead. items.title: Somalia: NISA Arrests 11 Al-Shabaab Operatives in Security Operations Around Mogadishu
items.description: NISA said its forces arrested 11 operatives linked to the networks, which were allegedly being prepared to carry out activities threatening security. The networks were dismantled during planned security operations conducted in Darussalam, Garasbaley, Kahda, Daynile, and Afgoye. NISA forces also seized weapons and other materials that the operatives allegedly intended to use in their planned activities. The operations are part of NISA's ongoing efforts to prevent Al-Shabaab and other terrorist groups from carrying out activities aimed at undermining security and harming the Somali people.
items.titleIt: Somalia: NISA Arrests 11 Al-Shabaab Operatives in Security Operations Around Mogadishu

items.description: The group that arrived in Mogadishu reportedly comprised 25 men and 25 women. items.titleIt: Somali-Turkish Tensions Rise as Deportations Follow Anti-Ankara Protests

items.titleIt: Somalia Mobilises for El Niño as Climate Risks Mount

items.title: The Signature That Never Comes: Why Somalia's Clan Killers Walk Free
items.description: A death sentence in Somalia isn't final until the president signs it. Increasingly, none of them do.   That piece traced how Ahmed Shire Hussein, a Somali National Army soldier, was executed on camera near El Baraf for the crime of his father's clan — one entry in a pattern of hit squads, informant networks, and a tribal shield strong enough that a court willing to execute Al-Shabaab fighters would not touch a killer protected by his own sub-clan. Why does almost no one ever pay for it? This is the answer: what decides whether the state acts is the relative political power of the clans in
items.titleIt: The Signature That Never Comes: Why Somalia's Clan Killers Walk Free

items.title: Somalia Awaits a New Security Order as Mission Drawdown Looms
items.description: The multilateral missions that have helped the Somali government fight Al-Shabaab for nearly two decades may be coming to an end. Mogadishu and its partners should get started now developing a plan for what they will do next.
items.titleIt: Somalia Awaits a New Security Order as Mission Drawdown Looms

items.title: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab
items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. To improve its lot, Mogadishu needs to bolster its military and alleviate civilian suffering in areas under insurgent control, while looking for openings for dialogue with the group.
items.titleIt: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab

items.description: The incident reportedly occurred at a residential facility. German authorities have identified a 28-year-old Somali man as the suspect. Police and prosecutors are investigating the circumstances of the incident, including the motive and whether it was connected to an earlier dispute between the two men. Moodey was a veteran journalist who worked in Somali media for many years. In 2014, he was arrested in Ethiopia and later sentenced to 27 years in prison under the country's anti-terrorism laws. items.title: Highlights of the Month from SJS Monthly Newsletter on Climate Change Reporting - August - September
items.description: El Niño Climate Impact Outlook – Somalia – UN OCHA Somalia's El Niño Climate Impact Outlook warns of a credible risk of severe flooding during the October–December 2026 Deyr season, particularly along the Jubba and Shabelle river corridors, if El Niño strengthens alongside a positive Indian Ocean Dipole. While the scenario is not certain, the outlook urges early action to address the combined risks of flooding, drought, extreme heat, disease, food insecurity, displacement, and infrastructure vulnerabilities. items.title: Somalia's Federal Member States Aren't Defending Sovereignty — They're Defending Their Patrons - No One in This Fight Is Neutral
items.description: Puntland is furious at Türkiye. Jubaland is furious at Türkiye. Both have spent the past five weeks accusing Ankara of killing their own people. Neither is in a position to make that accusation as a matter of principle. Puntland's ports are run by the UAE. Jubaland's survival for over a decade has depended on Kenya. The one Somali federal member state that tried to stand apart from any foreign patron — South West State — was crushed by federal troops within 48 hours in March. items.title: Somali-Turkish Tensions Rise as Deportations Follow Anti-Ankara Protests
items.description: The group that arrived in Mogadishu reportedly comprised 25 men and 25 women. items.title: Spike in online attacks silence Somali journalists in the midst of China and Turkey strategic communications partnership with Somalia
items.description: On Sunday, 13 September, at least three journalists and three media outlets reported they were affected by a fake memorialization campaign, account suspensions and content removals, leaving their platforms inaccessible to their audiences. According to exiled journalist Zakariye Mohamud Timacadde, his Facebook page, Zakariye Timacadde which has more than one million followers, was suspended around midnight on Sunday. items.title: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran
items.description: Egypt has been walking a tightrope since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began, joining mediation efforts while signalling solidarity with Gulf Arab partners under Iranian attack. But with some Gulf capitals voicing expectations of stronger support, Cairo may find itself under increasing pressure.
items.titleIt: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran

items.title: East Africa: Why the Int'l Community Must Confront TPLF Hardliners & Foreign Spoilers
items.description: [ENA] The signing of the Pretoria Permanent Cessation of Hostilities Agreement (CoHA) in November 2022 was widely hailed as a watershed moment for Ethiopia. After two years of devastating conflict in the northern part of the country, the agreement established a clear, lawful framework to restore constitutional order, demobilize combatants, deliver humanitarian relief, and rebuild shattered communities.
items.titleIt: East Africa: Why the Int'l Community Must Confront TPLF Hardliners & Foreign Spoilers

items.title: Ethiopia: Egyptian Minister's Remarks Reflect Crude Colonial Mentality - Ministry of Water and Energy
items.description: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Egyptian Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation recent statement suggesting that Ethiopians lack education is a manifestation of a crude colonial mentality that defines Cairo's policy in its relations with African states, Ethiopian Ministry of Water and Energy underscored.
items.titleIt: Ethiopia: Egyptian Minister's Remarks Reflect Crude Colonial Mentality - Ministry of Water and Energy

items.title: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany
items.description: According to a joint press release from the Darmstadt Public Prosecutor's Office and the South Hesse Police Headquarters, Mohamed Aweys Muudey, 68, an asylum seeker who had fled Somalia, was stabbed inside his communal accommodation by a 28-year-old suspect who is now in police custody. Muudey left Somalia in search of safety and protection. However, his life was cut short in a violent knife attack, highlighting the dangers many journalists in exile continue to face.
